answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and books one ledge in a canyon passage for one tide. The tide ledger lists ledge, key, and queue position, so an auditor recomputes the toll from position: the first pays 30, the kth pays 30+8(k-1), the 1000th pays 8022, and 1000 fakes lock 70000 plus pay 4026000 in tolls. A slot expires when its tide passes and cannot be banked or transferred. A rented-passage ring fails because a pass carries the owner key: a second key on the same ledge is rejected and both bonds burn. An honest agent books one ledge, pays 100 once, and recovers the bond after passage.
